Collect a fixed list of GET requests

Source: R/collect-gets.R
collect_gets.Rd

collect_gets() performs a fixed list of HTTP GET requests concurrently, respecting global and per-origin rate limits. It is designed for data platforms that collect from many sites at once: rate-limit waiting on one site never blocks requests to other, ready sites.

Usage

collect_gets(
  requests,
  type = NULL,
  max_inflight = 8L,
  max_inflight_origin = 2L,
  min_interval = 0,
  max_attempts = 3L,
  timeout = 30,
  default_retry_after = 1,
  user_agent = "tsibble (https://tsibble.tidyverts.org)"
)

Arguments

requests

A data frame with columns id (unique request identifiers), url (URLs to GET) and optionally type (declared response types); or a character vector of URLs, named with the request identifiers (positions are used as identifiers when unnamed).

type

The declared response type: "character", "double" (or "numeric"), "integer" or "logical"; a single value used for every request, or one value per request. A type column of requests takes precedence over this argument. Bodies are parsed strictly: "double" accepts decimal/scientific notation plus NA, NaN and Inf; "integer" accepts whole numbers in the integer range plus NA; "logical" accepts TRUE/FALSE/T/F (any case) plus NA; "character" takes the body as is.

max_inflight

Maximum number of requests in flight at once, across all origins.

max_inflight_origin

Maximum number of requests in flight at once per origin.

min_interval

Minimum number of seconds between consecutive request starts to the same origin.

max_attempts

Maximum number of attempts per request, including the first one.

timeout

Per-attempt timeout in seconds.

default_retry_after

Seconds to pause an origin for when a 429/503 response carries no usable Retry-After header.

user_agent

The User-Agent header sent with every request.

Value

An object of class collect_gets_result: a list with components

values

The parsed response values, in input order and named with the request identifiers. An atomic vector of the declared type when every request declares the same type, otherwise a list of typed values. Failed requests are NA here; see requests$ok.

requests

A data frame holding exactly one terminal state per request identifier: id, ok (TRUE when the request succeeded), status (the HTTP status code, NA when no response was received), reason (the HTTP reason phrase, or a description of the transport or response type error), attempts, origin and url.

Details

collect_gets() paces and retries the requests according to the rules below, and always returns one terminal state per request identifier.

Scheduling

  • At most max_inflight requests are in flight at any time across all origins, and at most max_inflight_origin per origin (an origin is the scheme, host and port of a URL).

  • Consecutive request starts to the same origin are spaced by at least min_interval seconds.

  • A 429 (Too Many Requests) or 503 (Service Unavailable) response pauses its origin until the time given by the Retry-After response header, which may be delta-seconds or an HTTP-date (default_retry_after seconds is used when the header is missing or cannot be parsed). The pause applies to every subsequent request to that origin, first attempts and retries alike, and a new Retry-After can only extend an existing pause, never shorten it.

  • Waiting requests hold no in-flight slot: while one origin is paused or throttled, requests to other ready origins continue.

Retries and terminal states

Requests are retried after 429/503 responses and after transport errors (e.g. timeouts or connection failures), up to max_attempts attempts in total. Other statuses — including redirects, which are not followed — are terminal immediately. Every request identifier ends with exactly one terminal state, reported in the requests component of the result.

Results

Successful (2xx) responses are parsed into the declared type and composed, in input order and keyed by id, into the native values vector. Failed requests keep their HTTP status and reason in requests and are NA in values; use requests$ok to tell a failed request apart from a legitimate NA, 0, FALSE or "" value. A response body that cannot be parsed as the declared type is a (terminal) response type error, reported in requests$reason.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
reqs <- data.frame(
  id = c("cats", "dogs"),
  url = c("https://example.com/api/cats", "https://example.org/api/dogs"),
  type = "double"
)
res <- collect_gets(reqs)
res$values
res$requests
} # }
